events.note: RESOLVED (re-examined at 0.25s resolution): the bat motion at ~9-11.5s is a load/reset, not a missed swing -- bat trails down at ~9.0, drops to a relaxed hang near the ground at ~9.5 (a real swing's follow-through wraps up across the body, it doesn't relax straight down), swings back up onto the shoulder at ~10.0, and is fully coiled/ready again by ~11.5, before the actual swing. That up-down-up cycle over ~2.5s reads as taking a pitch and resetting, not one continuous fast arc through the hitting zone. No separate missed-swing event needed. Ball clearly visible in flight right next to the bat at ~13, confirming contact; fielders converge in the infield ~13-15; runner visibly running toward first (right side of frame, where the base is) through ~15-16; runner and fielder together near the base at ~17, then both walk off casually by ~20, consistent with an out call. Defense back in standard positions by ~22-24.
events.stage11_note: Stage 11 acceptance criterion, NOT graded by Stage 10: play visually resolves (runner+fielder together at the base, about to walk off) at approximately t=18s. Stage 11 should report how close the kept segment's end lands to this mark.

base_occupancy.pixel_xy_note: read visually off the b1_t18 frame (fielder/runner standing at the base bag); not a real calibration click -- a placeholder for validating compute_occupancy before the Stage 10 UI exists.
base_occupancy.note: Stage 10 acceptance criterion. Runner+fielder converge and are both at/near the base from ~16-18s before walking off; the tag/out is judged to land at ~16.5s (fielder receiving the throw and applying the tag, before the pair starts moving away together at ~17). Precision here is inherently looser than the other timestamps in this file -- distant, small, motion-blurred figures at 1fps-equivalent review -- treat as +/-1s.
